_meta.purpose: The edha-items pack source (opened 2026-07-18, §9j rescope — Ben: mirror-and-own, same pattern as the heroic copy-in). THIS file holds the Edha-authored items: the kit pieces the system pack lacks, the trade-token characterization items, and Edha-specific objects (the Malcurr-stamped blade). The shipped cosmere-rpg.items gear gets copied IN here (re-priced c/s/g, Roshar-isms curated out) once Ben pastes scripts/items-dump-console.js and commits source-materials/edha-items-dump.json.
_meta.pricing: price.value + price.denomination ('copper'|'silver'|'gold') against the registered edha currency (canon §5d anchors: day's labor 1s, bread 1c, plain sword 2g). price.value 0 = not-for-sale story gear.
_meta.icons: Deliberately core Foundry SVGs (icons/svg/*.svg — guaranteed to exist; a 404 icon is invisible, §10 gotcha). Real art is a later art-pass swap.
_meta.mirror: 89 items mirrored from cosmere-rpg.items (dump 2026-07-18, system 2.1.0) at 3 mk = 10 c (longsword 60 mk = 2 g anchor). rawSystem = the shipped system subtree verbatim with only price + the description Price line re-denominated. _review lists Roshar-flavored entries for Ben to prune or re-flavor. Roshar MONEY loot (30 isMoney sphere/gem items) EXCLUDED — the registered edha currency replaces them (rulings 54/58).

items.name: Malcurr-Stamped Blade
items.description:
Malcurr mountain-forge work: a plain, well-made shortsword whose ricasso carries a forge-mark and assay-brand chain — in Malcurr a coin or a blade without its maker's credential is a lie, so the steel names its forge-town and striking-season to anyone who can read the marks (a Malcurri character reads them on sight). Matched sets of these have been turning up on the Palewater in the hands of soldiers whose own crown pays them in paper.

The session-1 clue object (canon §5d, ruling 57): trace the stamps north and ask who pays for matched armor on unpaid soldiers.

items.name: Bedroll
items.description: Waxed canvas and wool, rolled and strapped. A dry night's sleep anywhere you can lie down.

items.name: Mess Kit
items.description: Tin plate, cup, spoon, and a small pan that nest into one strapped bundle. Soldiers' issue across half the continent.

items.name: Snare Kit
items.description: Wire loops, cord, and stakes for a half-dozen small-game snares. Checked at dawn, reset at dusk; in famine country this is the difference between a kit and a meal.

items.name: Quiver (20 arrows)
items.description: A leather quiver holding twenty fletched arrows. Recover what you can after the fight — fletchers charge for what you don't.

items.name: Journal (blank)
items.description: A bound book of blank paper — not cheap, and worth it. In Goldenport what's written is what's real; in Canticle what's recorded outlives you.

items.name: Chalk (5 sticks)
items.description: Five sticks of white chalk. Marks walls, floors, sums, and the way back out.

items.name: Signal Horn
items.description: A brass-mouthed horn whose call carries over a fight, a river, or a mile of open ground. Every company learns its own calls; everyone learns rally and run.

items.name: Pennant
items.description: A long swallow-tailed flag on a socketed staff head — a rally point that can be seen when a horn can't be heard. Blank until your company has something to sew on it.

items.name: Written Commission
items.description: The formal record of a command you once held — the company named, the authority that signed it, and whatever became of both. (Leader kit token: write one line about the company — disbanded, dead, or left behind.)

items.name: Papers (genuine or otherwise)
items.description: Letters of passage, guild introductions, a customs chit with a smudged year — the right paper at the right checkpoint is a key, and in Goldenport's ledger-law it is very nearly a weapon. (Agent kit token: decide with the GM which of these are real.)

items.name: Trophy String
items.description: Teeth, feathers, a tollbird's ash-gray pinion — a hunter's résumé on a cord, read fluently by any border warden. (Hunter kit token: name the kill each piece came from.)

items.name: Regimental Token
items.description: A unit badge, a warband ring, a drill-hall coin — proof of where you learned the trade of arms, and a door-opener with anyone who served near it. (Warrior kit token: name the outfit.)

Every culture of Roshar has its own intoxicating traditions, such as beers, mudbeers, ciders, honu, shiki, juices, and lagers.

In Vorin society, almost all forms of alcohol are referred to as “wine” regardless of their ingredients. Such wines are known by their distinct colors, which are infused into each beverage so they can be distinguished at a glance. From least intoxicating to most, the types of wine are:

Color

Effect

Pink

Noted as being floral and aiding alertness.

Less intoxicating than milk

Orange

A non-intoxicating wine that tastes of fruit with notes of ginger. Most popular with members of the clergy.

Yellow

Offers a bold and deep flavor “without guilt.”

Minimally intoxicating

Auburn

Spicy with an earthy aroma. Brewed with fermented fruit.

Red

Flavorful wine with a pleasant burn.

Sapphire

Nutty with notes of honey, made with fermented lavis grain

Blue

Carries complex notes of berry and lemon.

Violet

Potent liquor with an aroma of spiced sandalwood.

Considered the most flavorful of the wines

Often manufactured using Roshar’s deadly blackbane plant, poison comes in single-dose glass vials. As 1 , you can pour it into food, liquid, or a container, or you can apply the poison to a melee weapon or a piece of ammunition you’re holding. When you do, the GM may require you to make a Stealth test to avoid discovery.
